message:
Thanks. To check which programmes you may qualify for, I need a few details. Please answer what applies:

1. How many people live in your household, including you? (1; 2; 3; 4; 5; 6; 7 or more)
2. How many children under 18 live with you? (none; 1; 2; 3; 4 or more)
3. If there are children, is any of them under 5? (no; yes)
4. Is anyone pregnant, or is there a baby under 1? (no; yes)
5. Does anyone have a disability? (no; yes)
6. Roughly how much does the household earn from work in a year, before tax? (none; $1 to $10,000; $10,000 to $20,000; $20,000 to $30,000; $30,000 to $40,000; $40,000 to $50,000; $50,000 to $60,000; $60,000 to $80,000; $80,000 to $100,000; $100,000 to $150,000; $150,000 or more)
7. Any other income a year, such as pensions, unemployment, interest, or child support? (none; $1 to $5,000; $5,000 to $15,000; $15,000 or more)
8. How much Social Security does the household get in a year? (none; $1 to $10,000; $10,000 to $20,000; $20,000 to $30,000; $30,000 or more)
9. What do you pay for rent or mortgage each month? (none; $1 to $500; $500 to $1,000; $1,000 to $1,500; $1,500 to $2,000; $2,000 to $3,000; $3,000 or more)
10. Roughly how much is in bank accounts and investments? (under $2,000; $2,000 to $5,000; $5,000 to $20,000; $20,000 to $100,000; $100,000 or more)
11. Does anyone get health insurance through a job? (no; yes)
reply: Just me. No, no children. No. No. I don't really know. Around $3,000 a month. $1,600 a year. None. $1,000 a month. A little cushion, not much. Yes, I'm on my company's plan.

message:
Thanks, that helps. Just to confirm two things:

1. Is the "$3,000 a month" your gross pay before tax, which comes to about $36,000 a year? (Yes; No, it's closer to: ...)
2. Are you self-employed, or do you work for an employer? (no; yes)
reply: Around $3,000 a month. I'm not sure.

summary: New Jersey, single adult in their thirties, no children, no pregnancy, no disability, no Social Security. Earnings about $3,000/month (about $36,000/year; gross vs. net unclear, but either way above limits). Other income about $1,600/year, rent about $1,000/month. Has job-based health insurance. Not eligible for: SNAP (gross income above the 200% FPL limit for 1 person), WIC, TANF, SSI, CHIP, school meals, child tax credit (no children), EITC (income above the childless limit), Medicaid (NJ adult limit about 138% FPL, roughly $22,000/year). ACA premium tax credit is unlikely because employer coverage is available; it would only apply if the employer plan were unaffordable or not minimum-value, which the person could check with their employer's plan cost. Self-employment status was not answered, but it would not change the result. No recommendation for any of the ten programmes.
